item.content:encoded:
That last line got me. +1

I'm suspending my disbelief that this sort of emotional stress would be subject to it's adaptability and either fade before it "wished it was dead" or adapted to break containment. That's the only problem I have with this- 682 is rather subdued as a narrative effect to make something (immortality) seem much worse, even for the lizard himself. It has been done before but I like this a bunch.

It is really just an elaborate single termination log which is fine- it is worlds better than the 076x682 termination log, imo. Good job!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Seconding this, and taylor's comment below. It's far too quick for its own good, resigning to a single day's event and rushing straight towards an attempt at pathos. I can't feel bad because there's no sense of time here to really let the weight of the scenario sink in.

It doesn't necessarily need to be any longer, per se, but the event could be better structured to give the impression it is, so the damn lizard's struggle doesn't feel entirely glossed over.

It feels low-effort, which is a shame, because it's a cool thing to focus on in the context of EOD. This treatment seems like a waste of a good idea.

Couple nitpicks, though I should mention they didn't really affect my vote

+ show block
– hide block

Every Monday, Wednesday and Friday, at 1500 hours on the dot, the door would open to 682's cell.

Personally feels too lolfoundation for me with how often it is - three times a week to pull out all the stops and go apeshit on the lizard? I would imagine, if indeed they're crazy dead-set on terminating it, it'd be more of a once-monthly thing. I wouldn't normally pick at this, but EOD hasn't to my knowledge been rediculous in terms of portraying the competence of SCPF operations.

Except today, they were late. Except they were never late.

I feel the second sentence here would pack a touch more punch if you dropped the redundant 'except'.

item.title: Counterpoint
item.content:encoded: I really like this format given the subject matter. I don't consider reptiles, particularly this lizard, capable enough of emotion that it's a necessary or even desired addition. And with the series 1, iconic nature of the subject matter, the fact that there isn't a lot of that secondary emotional narrative really emphasizes the 'cold, not cruel' nature of the foundation in that era. Letting the stark reality of the situation do the heavy lifting of informing you how to feel is something I generally get behind, and the comments here pretty much go with that, indicating that they feel bad for 682.

item.title: Yay, a Series I tale
item.content:encoded:
Impossible-to-Destroy Lizard? Alright.
SCP-682 tale? Oh, cool. Alright.
End of Death hub? Oh boy, here we go.

Every Monday, Wednesday and Friday, at 1500 hours on the dot, the door would open to 682's cell.

This was the only break from the monotony of containment that the lizard got. It wasn't much, but it was something.

… okay.

We had a good run.

… dang. I… shoot. Man.

The vat was cramped, but even worse — it was boring.

… Shit, man. That’s… a big bummer. Shit. It’s kind of sad.

The lizard wished it was dead.

FINE. TAKE IT. TAKE YOUR +1.
